paragraphs.text: Four fairies were moving into a secret grove.
They were new birthday fairies.
Their job was to grant children's birthday wishes.
"I'm unpacked!" Sprite said.
"Wow," Bumble said. "You're fast!"
"I'm going to make Fairy Grove look pretty," Feather said.
She hung wind chimes from a branch.
Then she wrapped ribbons around a tree.
"Looks nice," Hob said as he unpacked.
He yawned. "I wanted to be a tooth fairy.
That job is much easier."
Bumble flipped through a training book.
"I wonder when our first birthday wish will come."
He gulped. "What if I mess up?"
"Relax," Sprite said.
She snatched the book from Bumble and flew away.
"Hey!" Bumble called. "Give it back!"
"Come and get it!" Sprite said.
She zipped around, laughing.
Bumble flew after her.
He knocked into a branch. "Ouch!"
Bumble rubbed his head. "This job does seem hard."
Feather nodded. "We can't let any humans see us!"
Sprite laughed. "You three worry too much!"
She sat on a branch and kicked her legs.
"Being a birthday fairy will be fun."
"Maybe we should study the rules," Feather said.
Sprite giggled. "Who can catch the book?"
She darted away again.
Hob winked at the others.
"Sprite, you’re the fastest fairy ever," he called.
"None of us can catch you!"
Sprite landed in front of him.
"I am fast, aren’t I?" she bragged.
"Yes!" Hob took the book from her.
The fairies gathered around the book.
Feather started to read some rules.
"When a birthday fairy sees wish smoke—"
"Look!" Bumble cried.
Smoke drifted through the park and into Fairy Grove.
"Oh boy!" Bumble fell over with excitement.
"Here comes our first birthday wish!"
Bumble flew around in circles. "A wish!"
Feather watched the wish smoke.
"It's forming words!"
"A boy named Joey wants a bike," Sprite said.
The fairies looked at one another.
"What do we do now?" Hob asked.
Sprite checked the book. "We follow the smoke."
Hob groaned. "I hope it's not a long flight."
The smoke led to a house in town.
The fairies peered through a window.
"Joey and his family!" Bumble whispered.
Feather made a face. "Yuck.
He has an army cake. It's not very pretty."
Suddenly Joey's brother glanced up.
He looked right at the fairies!
"Hide!" Sprite cried.
She turned into a twig.
Feather turned into a feather.
Hob became a leaf.
Bumble took a deep breath.
"You can do this!" he told himself.
He turned into a mushroom.
Bruce rubbed his eyes.
"What's the matter, Bruce?" Joey asked.
"I thought I saw something," Bruce said.
"But it was nothing.
Mom, there's a mushroom on our window!"
"Don't be silly!" Joey's mom said.
Soon the fairies changed back to themselves.
They flew to a tree.
Hob moaned. "I told you this job was hard!"
Sprite rolled her eyes. "Let's go to the Wish Factory.
We can find out what to do there."
Blinx was in charge of the Wish Factory.
He glared at the fairies. "What do you want?"
"We have to grant a boy's wish," Sprite said.
"For a bike."
Blinx held out his hand. "Where's the wishbit?"
"Huh?" Bumble said. "Wishbit?"
Blinx rolled his eyes. "Didn't you read the training book?
I need something that belongs to the birthday kid.
Then I can make the gift.
Get something from him—and don't get caught!"
It was nighttime.
The fairies were outside Joey's house.
"How do we get in?" Bumble whispered.
"I see an open window," Sprite said.
"Come on!"
The fairies flew up to Joey’s room.
As they slipped inside, Bumble gasped.
"There are two beds.
This is Bruce’s room too!"
Just then Bruce rolled over.
He was talking in his sleep.
"Shh," Hob hissed. "Don't wake him!
Let's grab something and go!"
Feather spotted a shiny rock next to Joey's bed.
"That rock is pretty," she said. "Let's get it!"
"No!" Hob said. "That's too close to him.
Let's take something easy, like this."
He pointed to a book on the floor.
Bumble frowned as he looked around.
"How do we know what belongs to Joey?
Some of this stuff must belong to Bruce."
"Good point, Bumble," Sprite said.
Sprite flew around the room.
Then she pointed to a cabinet. "There!"
The name Joey was written on the door.
"He probably keeps his special things in there."
Feather helped Sprite open the door.
One shelf was filled with rows of tall toy soldiers.
"We can't take a soldier," Hob said.
"They're as big as we are!"
Sprite grinned and pulled a pouch from her pocket.
"Time for some shrinking powder!"
Sprite sprinkled powder on one soldier.
It shrank to the size of a button.
"Perfect!" Bumble reached for the tiny soldier.
Then— clunk! He knocked into a big one.
The big soldier crashed to the floor. Thud!
The fairies froze as Bruce sat up in bed.
He blinked in surprise. "Whoa!
Those tiny people are back!"
Bruce jumped out of bed.
"I'm going to catch you!" he growled.
He grabbed his pillowcase—and ran at the fairies!
"Fly, everyone!" Sprite cried. "Fast!"
She shot into the air.
But the other fairies were too slow.
Bruce tossed the pillowcase over them.
"Ha!" he cried. "Got you!"
"You can't get me!" Sprite yelled.
"Yes, I can!" Bruce chased her around the room.
Sprite zigzagged.
She darted high and dipped low.
She did flips and spins and then . . .
Sprite began to fly in a circle.
"Grr!" Bruce spun around, trying to catch her.
Sprite flew faster and faster.
Bruce spun faster and faster.
"Ahh!" Suddenly Bruce stopped.
"The room is spinning!"
Bruce was so dizzy, he dropped the pillowcase!
The three fairies flew out.
"Whew!" Bumble said. "I'm dizzy too!"
"Come on!" Sprite cried. "Let's go!"
The fairies brought the toy soldier to Blinx.
"What took you so long?" Blinx snapped.
He took the toy into a back room.
Soon Blinx was back.
"Return this soldier," he said.
"Then the boy's wish will appear."
Bumble gulped. "We have to go back to Bruce's house?"
"I hate this job!" Hob moaned.
Sprite took the soldier.
"We'll go first thing in the morning."
The next day the sun was shining.
Sprite flew to Joey's house with the soldier.
She put the toy down in front of the door.
Zap! The toy was its normal size again.
Sprite flew back to the other fairies.
"Look, Sprite!" Bumble cried.
A new bike sat near Joey's front door.
Feather shrugged. "It's army green, but Joey will love it."
When Joey opened the door, his eyes went wide.
"An army bike!" he cried. "Just what I wished for!"
"Aww." Hob brushed a tear from his eye.
"I love this job!"
Sprite rolled her eyes, but Bumble laughed.
"Me too!" he said.
Bumble watched Sprite fly through the air.
"I wish I could fly like you, Sprite," he said.
Sprite made a figure eight around Fairy Grove.
"I'll teach you, Bumble."
"Really?" Bumble jumped into the air.
He bumped into Feather's wind chimes.
"Oops, sorry!" he said. "I'm so clumsy!"
Feather sighed. "That's okay, Bumble.
You didn't break them—this time!"
Bumble flew after Sprite.
He tried to keep up with her.
But she was very fast.
Hob watched from his hammock.
"Stop blocking the sun!" he called.
Sprite rolled her eyes. "Hob, go back to sleep.
Bumble, fly faster."
Bumble bit his lip. "I'm afraid I'll bump into something."
"Be brave, Bumble," Sprite said.
"A good flier takes risks!"
Bumble closed his eyes.
Then— zoom!
He flew as fast as he could.
A second later he crashed into Sprite. "Oops!"
Both fairies crashed to the ground.
"Sorry!" Bumble cried.
Hob laughed. "Sprite, you forgot to teach Bumble something.
Keep your eyes open while flying!"
Sprite scowled at the lazy fairy.
Then she shot over to his hammock—and flipped it!
"Ow!" Hob cried as he tumbled onto the grass.
"That hurt!"
"A birthday wish!" Feather cried suddenly.
Wish smoke was drifting into Fairy Grove.
Hob got up and dusted himself off.
"I hope it's an easy wish," he mumbled.
"Me too!" Bumble said.
The fairies gathered around the wish smoke.
"It's from a girl named Sally," Feather said.
"She wants a friend."
"A friend?" Bumble scratched his head.
"Blinx can't make a person at the factory—can he?"
Sprite shrugged. "Let's follow the smoke.
We'll get a wishbit and learn more about Sally!"
The fairies followed the wish smoke to a house.
A big truck was parked out front.
Hob gulped. "Is that a moving truck?"
"I hope not," Sprite said.
The fairies flew over to a window.
Inside the house, movers were packing boxes.
The fairies looked at one another.
"Sally's family just moved out!" Feather said.
Bumble bit his lip.
"We need a wishbit for Blinx.
We can't grant Sally's wish without it."
Hob sighed and looked around.
"Let's go sit on that fence.
We can talk about what to do."
The fairies flew over to the fence.
"Sally's things must be in the truck," Feather said.
Sprite nodded. "We can search the boxes for a wishbit."
"What if we can't find anything?" Bumble asked.
"Calm down, Bumble." Sprite scratched her arm.
"We'll find a wishbit and bring it to—"
"Ahh!" Feather let out a cry. "My beautiful wings!
They're covered with bumps!"
Hob sneezed and scratched his nose. "I'm so itchy!"
"Me too. Ah-choo!" Bumble said, sneezing.
Bright red spots covered all the fairies.
"Oh!" Sprite looked down. "This fence is made of iron!"
"So?" Bumble said.
"Fairies are allergic to some metals," Sprite said.
"Like silver and iron!"
"Yikes!" Feather shot off the fence.
The other fairies quickly followed.
Soon their red bumps and sneezes faded.
"Whew!" Feather said.
"I was worried about my pretty wings."
"Shh!" Hob whispered. "Here come the movers!"
The fairies hid in some bushes.
They watched the movers carry more boxes to the truck.
"They're about to drive away!" Hob cried.
"We need to get a wishbit now !" Sprite said.
Suddenly— zoom!
Bumble shot into the truck.
And a mover slammed the doors!
The moving truck drove away.
Sprite hid her face in her hands.
"Why did Bumble fly into the truck?"
"You told him to be brave, remember?" Hob said.
"And fast," Feather added.
"It's all my fault!" Sprite moaned.
"Come on," Hob said. "Let's follow the truck."
The moving truck rumbled through town.
The fairies flew fast to keep up.
Finally the truck stopped in front of a house.
The three fairies flew to a tree.
Feather spotted a girl in the backyard.
"Look! That must be Sally!"
"She looks so sad and lonely," Hob said.
"I hope we can grant her birthday wish."
Sprite bit her lip. "We have to rescue Bumble first.
I'll be right back."
She took off and flew around the truck.
"Bumble!" she whispered. "Can you hear me?"
There was no answer.
Sprite was about to bang on the side.
But the movers began to unload the truck!
Sprite flew back to the tree.
The three fairies watched the movers.
The men carried box after box into the house.
"Where's Bumble?" Sprite whispered.
"Maybe he's in one of the boxes," Feather said.
"Let's go in the house.
We can look for Bumble—and a wishbit."
"Good idea," Hob said.
The fairies flew into the house.
Inside they saw stacks of boxes.
The movers carried things back and forth.
The fairies ducked into a room upstairs.
Sprite glanced around.
A few boxes had Sally's name on them.
"Yes!" she thought. "We can—"
"Meow!" A huge cat suddenly pounced on them!
Sprite changed into a twig.
Hob changed into a pebble.
Feather turned into a feather.
"Meow!" The cat purred happily.
It saw a new toy—Feather!
The cat smacked Feather with its paws.
Whap! Whap!
Feather flew all over the room.
Then the cat's sharp claws popped out!
"Ah-choo!" A loud sneeze startled the cat.
Bumble jumped from a box, covered with spots.
The cat hissed.
"Scat, Cat!" Bumble yelled. "Ah-ah-ah . . ."
Another giant sneeze burst from Bumble.
The cat jumped back and ran off!
The others quickly turned back into fairies.
Bumble grinned as he scratched a spot.
"There were some silver coins in the box.
But I found a wishbit." He held up a bookmark.
"I hope Blinx can help us with the wish."
The fairies flew to the Wish Factory.
The factory looked dark.
"Uh-oh," Hob said. "Where's Blinx?"
Blinx threw open the door. "Right here.
But I'm about to go home."
Bumble bit his lip. "A girl wished for a friend.
Can you help?"
Blinx sighed and took the bookmark.
A minute later he was back.
"Return this bookmark to Sally."
Then— boom! He shut the door.
The next day the fairies flew back to Sally's yard.
Bumble was holding the bookmark. "I hope this works."
Whoosh! A strong wind suddenly blew.
"The bookmark!" Bumble cried.
It blew out of his hand and past Sally.
"My bookmark!" she cried, running after it.
The fairies flew after Sally.
They followed her out of the yard.
Then they flew into another backyard.
"A unicorn bookmark!" someone cried.
Sally ran toward a little girl. "That's my bookmark!
It blew away."
The girl handed it to Sally. "I love unicorns too!
Want to play with me?"
Hob sighed happily. "Best friends forever!"
Sprite nodded. "Great job, Bumble.
You were fast—and brave!"
Bumble blushed. "And I didn't even break anything!"
"The Fairy Queen will be here soon!" Sprite said.
"I'm going to do a triple backflip for her.
She'll see what a good flier I am."
Bumble flew in circles.
"I'm so nervous about the test.
What if we mess up?"
"We'll pass the test," Hob said.
"We've granted several wishes.
And we've read the training book."
He smiled but his face was pale.
Feather twisted daisies into her hair.
"We'll just do our best," she said.
"Stop worrying!" Sprite said.
"We'll do better than our best."
The fairies suddenly heard trumpets.
Then bells tinkled, and swallows swooped through the air.
The swallows were pulling a carriage.
Bumble gasped. "She's here!"
The carriage landed in the grass.
The Fairy Queen stepped out.
"She looks stern," Hob whispered.
"I can make her smile," Sprite said.
"Birthday fairies!" the Queen said.
"I wish to know how well you are working.
So every season your team must pass a test.
Do well and you'll get a reward."
"What's the reward?" Feather asked.
"A feast at my palace," the Queen said.
Feather gasped. "That sounds wonderful!"
"Wh-what if we don't do well?" Bumble asked.
"You will fail the test," the Queen said.
"And lose your jobs."
Bumble gulped.
"Are you ready?" the Queen asked.
Sprite did a triple backflip and bowed.
"I can't wait to see your palace," she said.
The Queen frowned. "Let the test begin!"
Wish smoke instantly drifted into the clearing.
Sprite peered at the smoke.
"The wish is for ballet shoes."
"No," Feather said.
"It's for riding boots."
The fairies stared at the smoke.
Then they looked at one another.
"Uh-oh," Bumble whispered.
"For the test we have to grant two wishes!"
The Queen stared at Sprite. "This is a hard test."
"You bragged too much, Sprite," Hob whispered.
"She doesn't like you."
"What do we do?" Feather asked.
Sprite shrugged. "Just follow the wish smoke."
She zoomed off without the others.
"I will go too," the Queen said.
"I must see every part of your wish granting.
May I offer you a ride?"
The fairies climbed into the Queen's carriage.
The swallows darted into the air, lifting it.
"Your carriage is beautiful," Feather said.
Hob nodded. "This is the way to fly!"
The carriage followed the wish smoke to a garden party.
Sprite was sitting on a rosebush.
She frowned at the carriage.
"Why didn't I get a ride?"
"Sometimes it's better not to show off," Hob said.
Sprite stuck out her tongue.
Then she pointed to the birthday party.
"I understand the two wishes now."
Two identical girls stood near two cakes.
They wore matching dresses.
"Twins!" Bumble said.
Sprite nodded. "Let's get the wishbits."
Sprite flew into the house.
The others followed, even the Queen.
She was making notes in a notebook.
The fairies looked around.
Everything in the twins' room matched.
The Queen tapped a foot. "Please hurry.
I have a busy day."
Sprite finally grabbed two pairs of socks.
"Come on! Off to the Wish Factory!"
This time they all rode in the Queen's carriage.
The Queen quizzed them on the way.
"What makes fairies sneeze?"
"Iron and silver!" Feather said.
"What fruits are poisonous for fairies?"
"Limes and lemons!" Hob said.
The Queen paused.
"What's the most important part of a birthday fairy's job?"
"Easy!" Sprite giggled. "Stealing the birthday cake!"
"Wrong!" the Fairy Queen snapped.
"Your team has lost one point—for being silly!"
At the Wish Factory, Blinx bowed and bowed.
"It's good to see you, Blinx," the Queen said.
"I have many fairies to test today.
Can you make these gifts quickly?"
"Of course, Your Majesty!" Blinx said.
He hurried to the back.
"I've never seen Blinx act so nice," Feather whispered.
Hob chuckled. "Or so nervous.
He forgot the wishbits."
Blinx returned, his ears bright red.
"I forgot these," he mumbled, snatching the socks.
While the fairies waited, the Queen asked them more questions.
Feather, Hob, and Bumble were nervous.
Sprite was not.
"How do you hide from humans?" the Queen asked.
"Easy!" Sprite said. "You change shape.
I usually turn into a twig or pebble."
She turned into a pebble.
"You're too shiny," the Queen said.
"Humans will see you.
You've lost another point!"
"Sprite!" Hob hissed. "You're making us lose points!"
Feather frowned. "We'll never get the reward!"
Soon Blinx came back.
"The gifts will appear when you return the wishbits," he said.
"I put name stickers on the socks.
Remember—Kelly gets the ballet shoes.
Kendra gets the riding boots."
The fairies flew in the Queen's carriage again.
Sprite drummed her fingers.
"Flying like this is boring.
Watch me juggle the socks."
The Queen looked surprised. "You're going to juggle?"
"Yes!" Sprite tossed the socks in the air. "Oops!"
One name sticker fell off.
Then the other fell off too.
Bumble gasped. "Uh-oh!
Which pair of socks belongs to which twin?"
"Easy!" Sprite said.
"We'll just put the socks in the twins' room.
Their gifts will appear.
They'll each take the right gift."
The Queen folded her arms.
"That won't work.
You must give the right gift to the right twin.
If you do not, you will fail the test!"
Feather glared at Sprite. "This is your fault."
Bumble nodded. "We’ll fail the test because of you."
Sprite's lip quivered. "I'll fix it."
"Make sure no one sees you!" Hob said.
Sprite zoomed off to find the twins.
One was outside riding a toy horse.
"Kendra!" Sprite thought.
The other girl was inside, dancing to music.
On her bare feet, she spun around wildly.
"Kelly!" Sprite thought.
She looked closely at the socks.
One pair had two tiny holes.
The other pair looked brand-new.
"Easy!" Sprite grinned. "Kelly doesn’t like socks.
So the socks with holes belong to Kendra!"
Sprite dropped the brand-new socks near Kelly.
She dropped the socks with holes near Kendra.
"Phew!" she thought. "Nobody saw me."
Sprite flew back to the rosebush. "All done!"
"Are you sure?" Hob asked.
"Yes," Sprite said. "It was easy!
Now let's watch the gifts appear."
But outside no gift appeared.
Inside, no gift appeared either.
The Queen frowned. "Is there a problem?"
"No," Sprite said nervously. "Everything's great."
Sprite's heart was pounding.
Where were the birthday gifts?
Suddenly the twins' mother came inside.
"Kendra, turn the music down, please."
Sprite gulped. "Kendra?"
Sprite took off again.
Zipping around, she switched the socks.
Soon a shout came from the garden.
"Wow!" Kelly cried. "Ballet shoes!"
Then— clomp, clomp.
Kendra raced out in riding boots.
The fairies flew back to the carriage.
Sprite was huffing and puffing. "Did . . . we . . . pass?"
"Yes." The Fairy Queen nodded.
"But you did not earn the reward."
"Ugh." Sprite hung her head.
The other fairies groaned.
"You must be more serious, Sprite," the Queen said.
On the way home, the Queen leaned close to Sprite.
"Next time I come," she whispered.
"Will you teach me to juggle?"
Fairy Grove was green and peaceful.
The meadow near it was not.
A big machine was digging.
Workers were shouting.
The fairies watched from a tree branch.
Feather frowned. "Humans are ruining the meadow.
They're digging up all the pretty flowers."
Hob shrugged. "They're building a big playground.
Playgrounds are fun."
Sprite nodded. "I love slides!"
Feather shook her head. "Playgrounds are noisy."
Bumble bit his lip.
"What if the humans at the playground see us?
They might find Fairy Grove and—oops!"
He almost fell off the branch.
Sprite laughed. "Relax, Bumble.
We'll be safe."
"Humans can't find Fairy Grove," Hob said.
"It's hidden by magic."
"Playgrounds are ugly," Feather said.
"The meadow was perfect the way it was."
She sighed. "Those poor flowers!"
Sprite watched the two workers.
"Those workers take lots of breaks."
She poked Hob and giggled. "They're lazy—just like you!"
Hob frowned. "I'm not—"
"Look!" Bumble pointed toward Fairy Grove.
"Is that wish smoke?"
"Yes!" Sprite did a flip in the air. "Let's go!"
The fairies flew over fast.
Feather's face lit up as she read the wish.
"Ooh, pretty!
A boy named Bert wants a butterfly garden."
"Let's follow the wish smoke!" Sprite said.
The wish smoke led to a tall apartment building.
Hob pointed to the top floor.
"It looks like Bert lives up there."
"Uh-oh," Bumble said.
Outside the apartment, there was only a tiny balcony.
Down below there was no green grass.
The fairies looked at one another.
"Where will we put the garden?" Feather asked.
Hob shrugged. "Let's get a wishbit.
We'll bring it to Blinx.
He'll know what to do."
Bumble bit his lip. "I hope so."
The fairies peeked through the balcony doors.
Bert was eating birthday cake.
"Finish up, Bert," his dad said.
"We're going to the movies."
Bert's mom smiled. "A special birthday treat!"
Bert gulped down his cake. "Ready!"
Soon the family left.
The fairies found an open window.
"Here's Bert's bedroom," Bumble said.
"Wow!" Hob said.
"Bert really likes butterflies."
The fairies saw books about butterflies.
Butterfly models sat on a shelf.
Colorful butterfly posters covered the walls.
Feather found a tiny picture of a swallowtail butterfly.
"Perfect!" she said.
At the Wish Factory, Blinx was busy.
"I'm mixing potions and powders today," he snapped.
"Come back tomorrow!"
Feather shook her head. "We can't.
We have to grant a wish—today!"
Blinx grumbled, but he took the wishbit.
Blinx looked at the butterfly picture.
"A boy wants a garden?" He shook his head.
"My potions and powders aren't ready.
I can make flowerpots but no plants."
"What?" Bumble gasped.
"Then we can't grant Bert's wish!"
"We have to grant it!" Hob said.
"It’s his birthday!"
Blinx frowned. "Do you want the flowerpots or not?"
"No," Hob said.
"Yes!" Feather said.
They all looked at her.
"Humans dug up flowers in the meadow," Feather said.
"Let's bring those flowers to Bert.
We'll plant them in flowerpots on the balcony."
"Great idea!" Sprite said.
Blinx hurried off with the wishbit.
"There are workers in the meadow," Bumble said.
"What if they see us take the flowers?"
Hob folded his arms and nodded.
"We have to carry the flowers up to Bert's balcony.
That's too much work!"
Blinx returned and gave the wishbit to Feather.
"Put this back, and the flowerpots will appear.
Good luck—and good-bye!"
The fairies flew back to Bert's apartment.
Sprite returned the wishbit, and flowerpots appeared.
Feather clapped. "Now we just need the flowers.
Ready to fly back to the meadow?"
Bumble gulped. "C-can I stay here?"
"Me too," Hob said quickly.
Sprite rolled her eyes. "You're so lazy, Hob."
"It's fine," Feather said.
"You two can stay here.
Come on, Sprite.
You and I will get the flowers."
Feather and Sprite flew back to the meadow.
Now it was empty.
The big digging machine was quiet.
"Where are the workers?" Feather asked.
Sprite shrugged. "Maybe they're taking a break."
"Great," Feather said.
"Let's grab the flowers and get out of here."
The fairies flew around fast.
Feather picked her favorite flowers.
"We have enough now," Sprite said.
"Let's sprinkle shrinking powder on them and—"
Feather gulped. "A worker is coming!"
"Hide!" Sprite said.
Feather quickly turned into a feather.
Sprite turned into a twig.
They lay still on the ground.
A worker scratched his head and looked around.
"Hmm. I thought I saw something."
The other worker rolled her eyes. "Let's go, Joe.
We have work to do."
Rumble! Rumble!
The digging machine started up again.
It rolled across the meadow.
Its big shovel clanked, scooping up grass and plants.
Suddenly the digging machine turned.
Sprite heard it grow louder.
"It's coming toward us!" she thought.
Rumble! Rumble!
The digging machine grew louder and louder.
Clank! Its long shovel shot out.
It scooped up dirt—and both fairies!
Clank! Clank! The digging machine dumped its shovel.
Feather and Sprite tumbled into the dirt.
More dirt poured on top of them!
"Oh no!" Feather thought.
"We're getting buried in the dirt!"
Sprite felt more dirt fall on her.
But then the machine grew quieter.
"The machine is leaving," she said.
"Let's go, Feather!"
Feather and Sprite turned back into fairies. "Phew!"
They climbed out of the dirt.
Feather coughed and spat out dirt.
"Are you okay?" Sprite asked.
Feather brushed dirt off her wings.
"I'm fine," she said.
"Let's get away from here!"
Soon Sprite and Feather were back at Bert's apartment.
Feather planted the flowers on the balcony.
Sprite poked Hob. "What have you been doing—sleeping?"
"No!" Hob snapped. "We've been busy."
"We learned all about butterflies," Bumble said.
"Did you know they drink from mud puddles?
And they have really long tongues!"
Feather patted the dirt around the last flower.
"The garden looks beautiful.
Soon the butterflies will come!"
"Um . . ." Bumble stared at the flowerpots.
"You got the wrong kind of flowers.
Butterflies don't like those flowers."
Feather's wings drooped.
"We have to go back to the meadow?"
"No." Sprite pointed to Hob and Bumble.
"You two learned which flowers butterflies like.
You can go back to the meadow!"
Bumble and Hob sighed and flew off.
They soon returned.
In their arms were lots of colorful flowers.
"That was quick," Feather said.
